323, 504, 506, R/W 34 OF IPC ON THE COMPLAINT OF 2ND RESPONDENT BEFORE THE II ADDL. C.J. (JR.DN) AND JMFC,
GULBARGA WHICH IS PRODUCED AT ANNEXURE A AND B.
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The FIR was registered against the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A 323, 504 and 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
The registration of the FIR is impugned in this petition.
2. The summary of the charge sheet is that, the De-facto complainant is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1 and accused No.2 is the mother-in-law.
Since one year prior to the date of lodging of the FIR, the De-facto complainant is residing in her parental home due to the cruelty meted out by the accused.
On 14.11.2021, the petitioners- accused Nos.1 and 2, who are residing in Bengaluru came to the parental home of the De-facto Complainant and assaulted her and also abused her in filthy language.
3. The learned Magistrate after accepting the charge sheet, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.
Taking exception of the same, this petition is filed.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that, the alleged incident has taken place on 14.11.2021 and the FIR was lodged on 18.11.2021 without offering any plausible explanation.
The material produced along with the petition discloses that, as on the date of incident, the petitioners were residing in Bengaluru.

He further submits that except omnibus and general allegations, there Fuzail Ansari And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4553064/
2 are no specific allegations so as to constitute the commission of the aforesaid offences.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that, the veracity of the allegations made against the petitioners-accused can be considered after full fledged trial.

Hence,
the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate does not warrant any interference.
6. Learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State would reiterate the submissions made by learned counsel for respondent No.2.

7. Considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
8.
In the FIR, the De-facto complainant has specifically stated that, she is residing in her parental home since one year prior to the date of lodging of the FIR.
It is alleged that on 14.11.2021, the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2, who are residing in Bengaluru came to her parental home and assaulted her and abused her in filthy language.
The petitioners-accused have produced the comprehensive full body checkup of accused No.2, which discloses that accused No.2 had undergone medical checkup on 14.11.2021 i.e., the date of incident.
The said document has neither been disputed, nor controverted by the respondents.

9. Perusal of the FIR discloses that except omnibus and general allegations against each of the accused, there is no specific allegation as to how the accused abused and assaulted the De-facto complainant.
The dispute between the parties arises out of marital discord, however, given a criminal texture with an ulterior motive to wreak vengeance and with revengeful intent.

No material is placed along with the charge sheet that the De-facto complainant had sustained simple injuries due to the alleged assault made by accused Nos.1 and 2, and in the absence of any material, the cognizance taken by the Magistrate for the offence punishable under Section 323 of IPC is without any substance.
10. In view of the above, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii.

The impugned First Information Report in Crime No.0031/2021 registered by Kalaburagi Women Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A,
323, 504 and 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC is hereby quashed.
iii. In view of disposal of the petition, pending interlocutory applications, if any, do not survive for consideration.
